 ‘Honestly, they don’t have anybody’ – Derek Fisher reveals his biggest fear for the LA Lakers this season
 Dan Coombs
 Tue 17 November 2026 18:22 GMT · 2 min read Add to Preferred Sources Photo by Meg Oliphant/Getty Images Add to Preferred Sources 
 Former Los Angeles Lakers player Derek Fisher is intrigued to see how the LA Lakers fare without one of their big names. 
 The LA Lakers have proven they can win without Austin Reaves. Luka Doncic just steps up with even more firepower.
 The Lakers have even shown they can win without Doncic, with Reaves leading a recent victory over the Pistons.
 But can they win without star center Walker Kessler?
 Kessler has been ruled out of the Lakers’ game against the Charlotte Hornets with lower leg soreness. Reaves will also miss the game.
 Speaking to 97.1 The Fan former player Derek Fisher is concerned that the Lakers lack a proper replacement for Kessler.
 “Honestly, they don’t have anybody,” he responded when asked who could fill in.
 Kevon Looney was so bad in his early season minutes that he has been a DNP in eight of the Lakers’ past 10 games.
 Samu Mamukashvili can move to center but this feels like only a stop-gap solution. Eventually they may need to lean into the trade market.
 TalkingPoints Which NBA teams are too reliant on their superstar? 💬
 Fisher: Lakers must learn to play small 
 Derek Fisher explains that the only real solution available to coach JJ Redick is for the Lakers to embrace the small-ball philosophy.
 He said: “Leaning into their smaller line up is what they are going to have to do. They don’t have a choice.
 “You lose some of that rim protection and shot blocking that he [Kessler] brings. You also lose a certain threat in pick-and-roll. He has shown an ability to play in pick-and-roll where he’s receiving the ball and able to spread it out. It’s also his threat at the rim, when he’s in the dunker spot, he can go get it.
 “Sometimes you have to figure out a way to play small, that’s part of why the coaching staff has been doing that this season, because they know they are going to need to know how to play with that smaller lineup.”
 The Hornets are not the most physical team in the paint, so the Lakers may like their chances of getting through this one without Kessler.
 But if he were to miss substantial time, there is no real solution.
 And considering that Kessler missed almost all of last season for the Jazz with an injury, the Lakers are taking a real risk by not having an adequate backup.
